agent: The illustration depicts an autonomous AI agent as a self-driving workshop: a human hand at the top places a single goal card into an inbox and then withdraws, leaving the machine to work; inside, a central orchestration engine expands the goal into a branching plan with decision diamonds and looping arrows that revisit earlier outputs for inspection. The engine reaches out to a bank of tools—a magnifying glass over a search bar, a code editor with typed syntax, a testing rig—and in one panel a small agent runs a script and checks the result before proceeding. Other agents work alongside, passing notes to one another in parallel, forming a swarm, while one minor branch follows a strict, pre-labeled script and another chooses its own path, showing the range of independence. A glowing progress bar and a power gauge indicate long-running computation consuming resources. The final output is not a single reply bubble but a shelf of completed research memos, test results, and graphs, with no further human input required.
frontier-model: The illustration depicts a vast, dark landscape under a starry sky, dominated by a glowing, jagged line cutting across the horizon like a moving frontier. On the near side of the line stand several sleek, metallic monoliths labeled with benchmark scores, each representing a released frontier model; they cast long shadows and are illuminated from above. Beyond the line, partially hidden in mist and behind a translucent curtain, loom much larger, shadowy versions of these monoliths with blurred labels and question marks—these are the unreleased frontier models that are more powerful than anything public. The ground in front of the line is littered with gold coins, power cables, and energy meters, conveying the enormous cost of training and running these systems. From the tips of the shadowy monoliths, tendrils of new abilities—glowing sparks, unfinished equations, and strange symbols—spiral upward. In the foreground, small groups of researchers in lab coats and government officials use telescopes, clipboards, and monitoring equipment to watch both the visible line and the hidden models beyond, their expressions tense and attentive. The line itself is not fixed; arrows and motion lines along its edge show it shifting forward as new models appear, and the whole scene is bathed in a cool, analytical light that conveys both awe and caution.
millennium-prize-problems: An illustration depicting a grand marble hall with seven imposing pedestals, each holding a glowing, intricate geometric puzzle box; six of the boxes are locked with heavy chains and padlocks, their surfaces covered in dense equations and question marks, while the seventh, labeled “Poincaré Conjecture,” sits open with its solved mechanism visible and a soft golden light spilling out. Suspended above each pedestal is a large price tag reading “$1,000,000,” but a stern panel of robed mathematicians with magnifying glasses and clipboards stands between the viewer and the boxes, examining a stack of documents on a desk; one of the mathematicians holds a crumpled paper labeled “Blog Post” and shakes their head, while a large hourglass on the desk marked “2-Year Scrutiny” is still running, and a banner overhead reads “Millennium Prize Problems: Seven Challenges, One Solved, Six Remain Open—Only Peer-Reviewed Proofs Collect the Prize.”
navier-stokes-equations: A single illustration shows a large, continuous fluid scene: translucent blue water at the bottom and pale sky at the top flow together around a silver aircraft wing, with curved streamlines and color gradients representing velocity, pressure, and viscosity. Across the image, the Navier-Stokes equations are written in white mathematical notation, linking the flow fields. At the center, one set of streamlines bends into a tight spiral that ends in a small, intensely bright point labeled blow-up?, with a crackling, impossible-looking energy. Hovering nearby is a small, glowing Millennium Prize medal, and faint background outlines of a weather map, an ocean wave, and a wind turbine connect the equations to weather prediction, ocean currents, and engineering. The contrast between the smooth, laminar regions and the singular point visually poses the open question of whether the equations always guarantee smooth solutions or can develop a blow-up.
token: A single illustration in the style of a cutaway diagram shows a pipeline from text to computation: at left, the word unbelievable is split by scissors into three colored blocks labeled un, believ, and able; these blocks roll on a conveyor into a stylized AI engine made of neural-network nodes, where they mix with streams of code and inter-agent speech bubbles that are also chopped into token blocks; from the engine's right side, a torrent of small coin-shaped output tokens pours into a giant hopper labeled billions or trillions of tokens, while a nearby meter counts output tokens and a price sticker reads per token; behind the machine, a chalkboard wall is covered with rough-work calculations, and a supervisor's clipboard shows that the total token count is used to measure how much computing the model has done, making the picture a self-contained explanation of tokens as countable, billable chunks of AI work.
